jobs.title: Perception Intelligence Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Opportunity

Brunswick Group is seeking a Senior Manager to join our Perception practice in New York.

Perception Intelligence is a part of Brunswick's Financial Practice and helps companies understand how investors, analysts, and other key stakeholders assess their strategy, management, communications, and long-term investment proposition. Through in-depth interviews and analysis, we provide actionable insights that help clients strengthen relationships with the capital markets and make better-informed communications and business decisions.

As a Senior Manager, you will lead perception studies, advise clients throughout the project process, develop strategic recommendations, and present findings to investor relations teams, executive management committees, and Boards of Directors. You will contribute to business development efforts, collaborate closely with colleagues across other practice areas, and support the continued growth and development of the Perception Analytics practice.

About the Role

Client Contribution and Project Execution

• Lead the execution of multiple concurrent perception studies while owning project oversight and quality control across the project team.

• Serve as a trusted advisor to clients on project scope and design, translating their objectives and priorities into a project framework.

• Develop and own client relationships, including sales pitches, day-to-day counsel, and debrief discussions.

• Conduct in-depth, virtual interviews with senior personas at investment firms to gather meaningful feedback.

• Analyze and interpret interview feedback to write summaries and translate them into clear strategic themes and recommendations for Investor Relations teams.

• Apply analytical rigor and strategic judgment in presenting data and findings to clients.

• Organize data, charts, and graphs in Excel and findings in PPT deliverables that are Board-ready.

• Present and discuss findings with senior audiences, including investor relations teams, executive management committees, and Boards of Directors.

Teamwork and Collaboration

• Serve as a subject matter expert across the firm on perception analytics.

• Mentor and develop junior colleagues, supporting professional growth across the team.

• Foster a collaborative, high-performing environment that promotes accountability, excellence, and continuous improvement.

Business Development

• Lead and contribute to business development efforts, including sales campaigns, proposals, and pitches.

• Contribute to internal initiatives, marketing programs, and thought leadership.

• Collaborate with colleagues across the firm to identify opportunities for integrated client solutions.

What We’re Looking For

At Brunswick, we seek intellectually curious, commercially minded individuals who combine strong analytical skills with sound judgment and excellent communication. We value professionals who can build trusted client relationships, lead complex engagements, and contribute to the development of colleagues and the wider business.

Standout Perception Senior Manager candidates will demonstrate:

• 5-8 years of relevant experience in perception research, investor relations, strategic communications, capital markets, equity research, or a related advisory environment.

• Strong understanding of capital markets, institutional investors, sell-side analysts, and the factors that influence investment decision-making.

• Experience in managing complex client engagements and overseeing multiple workstreams simultaneously.

• Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to high-quality output.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Demonstrated ability to build credibility with senior client stakeholders.

• Experience mentoring and developing junior team members.

• Commercial awareness and an interest in supporting business development.

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and collaborative environment.

Why Join Us

Joining Brunswick unlocks a range of exceptional employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.

The successful applicant will be eligible for the following compensation and benefits package:

Base Pay: The annual base compensation range for this role is $120,000-150,000. The base pay offered will be determined by factors including experience, skills, training, office location, certifications, and education.

Bonus Eligibility: Annual discretionary bonus contingent upon individual and firm-wide performance.

Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance. Disability insurance. Employee assistance program. Flexible spending account. Health savings account. Life insurance. Commuter Benefits. Generous Paid Time Off: 25 vacation days and 10 days sick leave, as well as 11 paid company holidays. Firm-sponsored 401(k) Plan with 3% automatic company contribution of base and bonus with an additional 1.5% profit share– immediate vesting. Career training and development opportunities. Employee discounts.

Office Policy: At Brunswick, our work is a craft that thrives in teaching environments – whether in our offices or on-site with clients – through real-time observation, collaboration, human connection, clear guidance and by challenging one another to keep getting better. Our policy is that our team members are in person – either in the office or on-site with clients – at least four days each week.

The firm will provide reasonable accommodation to qualified applicants or employees, as defined by applicable law. In addition to the application, the process may include virtual and in-person interviews, as well as an assessment, which may be timed. To request an accommodation during our application and hiring process, email americasaccommodations@brunswickgroup.com.

About Brunswick's New York Office

Brunswick’s New York Office is the largest of the firm’s six offices in the Americas. The office is home to approximately 250 colleagues working across the full range of Brunswick’s sector and practice groups, as well as our Insight, Digital and Creative teams.

Located in the heart of one of the world’s leading capital markets centers, Brunswick’s New York office serves as a global center of excellence for our Financial Institutions sector team – which advises leading banks, asset managers and insurers on a wide array of critical issues from corporate positioning to litigation and crisis – and our Financial practice – which advises clients across industries on M&A transactions, shareholder activism, investor relations and financial communications, IPOs, restructurings and ESG.

Our newly renovated and expanded space encompasses the 24th and 25th floors in the Grace Building on Bryant Park and serves as a convening space for Brunswick’s global colleagues, clients, media and other members of the business, political and social communities.

About Brunswick

Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes.

Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world.

Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please read our Global Privacy Notice to understand how your data is managed.

As a Peloton Expert, you are passionate about fitness, technology, and all things Peloton. Reporting to a Store Manager, you provide excellent in-store experiences and sales support within our retail stores. You educate visitors on the portfolio of Peloton products and content, creating meaningful interactions, customized solutions, and closing sales. You are proud to represent Peloton and find great satisfaction in helping others become Peloton Members!

• Provide excellent service and solutions to all current and future Members

• Stay current with new products, features, and content

• Meet or exceed established performance goals

YOU BRING TO PELOTON

• You are approachable, a good listener, and empathetic

• You have sales, service, or fitness experience in a customer-centric environment

• You have the ability to create immersive customer experiences

• Strong verbal and written communication skills

• You are ambitious, hardworking and team-oriented

• You are flexible with your schedule, including the ability to work evenings, weekends, and holidays

• Passion for health and wellness

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This is primarily an active position, involving long periods of standing and walking in the store, as well as bending and lifting items weighing 25 lbs or more. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, including H-1B transfers.

#LI-CM1

• Medical, dental and vision insurance

• Generous paid time off policy

• Short-term and long-term disability

• Access to mental health services

• 401k, tuition reimbursement and student loan paydown plans

• Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Pet insurance and so much more!

$19—$19 USD

At home, outdoors, traveling, or at the gym, Peloton brings together innovative hardware, distinctive software, and exclusive content. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City, Peloton has millions of Members across the US, UK, Canada, Germany, Australia, and Austria. For more information, visit www.onepeloton.com.

Peloton is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. jobs.description:
Our team of talented individuals is what makes us successful. To support our team, we provide a balanced mix of benefits and programs. Your total rewards package includes competitive pay, benefits, and perks, flexible work-life balance, professional development opportunities, and performance and recognition programs. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability, voluntary benefit programs (critical illness, hospital, and accident), health savings and flexible spending accounts, and retirement 401K plan. One of our fundamental principles is to offer competitive health and welfare benefits to our team members, providing coverage and care for you and your family. Full-time employees working at least 30 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefits and paid leave programs.  We pride ourselves on our collaborative work environment and culture, which embraces our mission of providing financial and non-financial benefits back to the members of the Seneca Nation.

Seneca Holdings is seeking a Sr. Project Controls Analyst. This is a remote opportunity. The Senior Project Controls Analyst plays a critical role in supporting the successful delivery of projects by assisting in the planning, execution, and closure phases. The position is responsible for coordinating and monitoring project billings, purchase orders execution, and resource management; monitoring financial performance; and tracking project setup while ensuring alignment with defined requirements, scope, and objectives. The Senior Project Controls Analyst serves as a key liaison between stakeholders, providing regular updates and facilitating communication across all participants. They maintain detailed project documentation and track project performance to ensure internal standards are met. Additionally, the role involves managing risks, resolving issues, escalating concerns when necessary, and supporting the Project Manager in the day-to-day operations of the project.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Prepare, organize, and submit comprehensive project setup documentation in accordance with internal guidelines and contract requirements.

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date project files, including setup forms, billing requests, customer invoices, and other relevant documentation to ensure audit readiness and operational efficiency.

• Generate and submit customer billing requests and monitor their status through completion. Review invoices for accuracy and secure appropriate internal approvals prior to submission.

• Assist in the preparation of Purchase Order (PO) requests with Project Manager. Review submissions for completeness, including verification of charge numbers and General Ledger (GL) account coding.

• Enter approved Purchase Orders into Costpoint and maintain accurate records of all modifications.

• Monitor outstanding commitments with vendors and subcontractors to ensure alignment with project budgets and timelines.

• Track, report, and analyze key project and cost data—including funding, revenue, billing, unbilled amounts, and open commitments—providing timely insights to stakeholders.

• Develop, maintain, and analyze detailed Estimates at Completion (EACs) for assigned projects, identifying trends, risks, and variances from original proposed budgets and forecasts.

• Participate in EAC review meetings with Project Managers and stakeholders to assess project performance, staffing requirements, and potential funding risks.

• Attend internal project kick-off meetings to gather necessary data for new contract setup and ensure accurate implementation of project setup.

• Prepare detailed Project Setup Forms based on contract awards, ensuring accurate configuration of employee and vendor workforce data, labor categories (LCATs), and billing rates.

• Execute special projects and additional responsibilities as assigned.

• Conduct all business activities in full compliance with Seneca’s policies, procedures, and ethical standards.

Basic Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or business disciplines and 10 years of experience is preferred (13 years of experience in a budgeting, finance, or project control related field in lieu of Bachelor's degree).

• Hands-on experience with Deltek Costpoint and Business Intelligence (Cognos), for financial and data analysis.

• Extensive experience in government contracting with a strong understanding of various contract types, including Firm Fixed Price (FFP), Time and Materials (T&M), and Cost Reimbursable agreements.

• Proven ability to manage and support large, complex contracts with multiple Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) and diverse revenue streams.

• In-depth knowledge of Estimate at Completion (EAC) development, including associated financial analysis processes and procedures.

• Demonstrated strength in analytical thinking and problem-solving, with a focus on identifying trends, risks, and cost efficiencies.

• Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, with advanced expertise in Microsoft Excel for data analysis, reporting, and financial modeling.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and concisely.

• Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and levels of the organization.

• Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a self-motivated approach and the ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Brokerage Operations
As Savvy launches its broker-dealer, this role will be responsible for building and owning the following functions end-to-end:

 - Build and run the end-to-end operational workflow across the brokerage lifecycle, resolving issues as they arise

 - Establish a process for monitoring post-trade activity and resolving issues before they become bigger problems

 - Create the workflow for investigating and correcting errors, and keeping records reconciled and accurate

 - Build the framework for managing corporate action communications

 - Establish quality-control review processes and documentation to ensure we're meeting our obligations

 - Build the workflow for supporting regulatory reporting requirements across product types

 - Identify opportunities to deploy AI tools and agentic workflows to automate reconciliation, exception detection, and error-resolution processes

Account & Cashiering Operations

 - Design and run the workflow for reviewing, approving, and processing client money movement requests, including domestic and international transfers

 - Build and maintain monitoring processes to flag anomalous account activity and ensure timely escalation

 - Establish a repeatable process for managing deposits end-to-end, from receipt to posting

 - Create and refine the process for triaging and resolving new account setup exceptions

 - Build the framework for maintaining and updating account restrictions, ensuring accuracy across systems

 - Leverage AI and automation to streamline approval workflows and flag anomalies faster and more accurately

 - Support the Legal & Compliance team with FINRA and audit requests

 - Prepare client complaint and resolution reports

 - Explore AI-driven tools and agentic workflows to reduce manual effort in reporting and audit preparation

 - 3-5 years of total experience across investment banking, consulting, or fintech startups

 - Strong process orientation: able to build SOPs and controls where none exist today

 - Comfortable partnering across Investment Operations, Compliance/Legal, and Product/Engineering

 - Comfort using AI/automation tools to reduce manual reconciliation and exception-detection work

 - Experience at a high-growth fintech or startup, or building an operations function from the ground up

 - Prior experience at an introducing broker-dealer or clearing firm (e.g., Fidelity NFS, Pershing, Apex)

 - Working knowledge of the trade lifecycle

 - Understanding of FINRA/SEC compliance reporting requirements

 - SIE, Series 7, 24, and 99

THE ROLE:

Savvy is scaling fast, and the transition team is how new advisors get from signed to fully live on our platform. As a Senior Client Transition Specialist, you will own the most complex advisor book transitions end-to-end (large books, advisor teams, Broker Protocol moves, multi-custodian repapers) and act as an extension of the Onboarding Manager across every onboarding in flight. You will set transition plans, assign and balance work across the specialists, coach them day to day and assist the Onboarding Manager with people management (formal direct reports expected in 2027), partner with the manager on complex issues and escalations, and build the processes and automation that let the team absorb more advisors without adding headcount at the same rate. You will run your own book and raise the bar for everyone else's.

Who you are:

 - You've done this before. You've owned advisor transitions end-to-end at a custodian, RIA, broker-dealer, or fintech, and you know what breaks a repaper or an ACAT before it breaks.

 - You're a step ahead. You see which transition is about to slip before anyone says so, and you act on it.

 - You're detail-obsessed, and you spread it. You catch the error others miss, and you teach the people around you to catch it too.

 - You make calls. Given incomplete data and a go-live date, you decide what blocks, what waits, and who needs to know, without waiting for permission.

 - You build leverage. You turn a one-off fix into a repeatable workflow, document it, and use AI as a default tool while knowing exactly when to verify it.

 - You communicate directly. You keep advisors, custodians, and teammates calm and informed under pressure, and you say the hard thing early.

 - You have a humble, “can do” attitude and extreme ownership. You want to be part of a winning team, and you embrace being pushed out of your comfort zone.

You will report to the Client Service Onboarding Manager.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the end-to-end transition of Savvy's most complex advisor books across custodians (Schwab, Fidelity), from transition planning and paperwork generation through completed account transfers and handoff to steady state.

 - Act as an extension of the Onboarding Manager: own assignment of new onboardings to specialists based on complexity and capacity, maintain visibility across all in-flight onboardings, run the weekly portfolio review, and rebalance work as risks and volume shift.

 - Solve complex issues and escalations (NIGO, custodian, vendor, data, advisor) together with the Onboarding Manager: own the first response, resolve or route quickly, and keep the advisor informed throughout.

 - QA paperwork, transition spreadsheets, and trackers on high-risk books before submission; run root-cause reviews on NIGOs and turn findings into fixes.

 - Assist the Onboarding Manager with people management of the Transition Specialists: regular 1:1s, coaching on process, custodial platforms, and judgment calls, performance input, and onboarding new team members. Formal direct reports expected in 2027.

 - Lead pre-go-live transition planning with Sales and the advisor's team: data readiness, sequencing, standing instructions, and go-live risks.

 - Own and maintain the transition playbook; identify, build, and document process and automation improvements (including AI workflows) in partnership with Product and Operations.

 - Report on transition health (turnaround, NIGO rate, stalled accounts) and flag risk early to leadership.


MUST HAVE:

 - 5 to 8+ years in client operations, advisor transitions, onboarding, or account management in wealth management, with at least one full advisor book transition owned end-to-end.

 - Hands-on experience with Schwab and/or Fidelity custodial platforms and a deep grasp of account transfer, repaper, LPOA, and ACAT paperwork and NIGO resolution.

 - A track record of operating across many concurrent, deadline-driven workstreams and seeing risk before it surfaces.

 - Demonstrated judgment: you've made consequential calls with incomplete information and can explain how you decided.

 - Experience coaching, training, assigning work to, or QA'ing the work of others, with or without formal authority, and the desire to manage people formally.

 - Strong data hygiene and spreadsheet skills (lookups, validation, cleaning messy custodian exports) and the discipline to catch errors before they compound.

 - At least one process or automation improvement you built that other people adopted.

 - Fluent, daily use of AI tools for data and document work, with clear judgment about when to trust versus verify output.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the confidence to keep advisors and custodians calm and informed under pressure.

 - A collaborative, low-ego, self-starter attitude with extreme ownership, and comfort in a high-growth, constantly changing environment.


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with Broker Protocol transitions, advisor teams, or books over $100M.

 - Familiarity with Orion, Salesforce, DocuSign, and bulk onboarding or CRM import tooling.

 - Experience building workflows or automations with AI tools (Claude, custom skills, scripts) beyond single-chat use.

 - Prior experience at a high-growth startup, custodian, RIA, or broker-dealer.

 - Experience formally managing a small operations team.

Savvy Wealth is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that values diversity and individual contributions.

A Note from your Future Manager

Hi! I’m Lauren & I lead Talent at Savvy. I’m hiring someone to join my team and wanted to share a little about what I’m looking for and what you can expect from us.

I’m looking for someone who’s motivated to keep getting better, curious enough to ask one more question, and resourceful enough to try a different approach when something isn’t working. We celebrate wins big & small, and recognizing each other’s work is part of our DNA.

You’ll work alongside incredibly talented people who are generous with what they know, open to new ideas, and excited to help each other succeed.

My hope is that you’ll look back on this role and be proud of the people you hired, how much you learned, and what we all built together.

If that sounds like the kind of team you want to be part of, I’d love to meet you.



The Role:

We’re hiring a Senior Talent Partner to help build teams across Savvy. You’ll own searches from intake through close starting with GTM, Operations, and G&A with room to expand into other parts of the business as we grow. 

You’ll learn what makes each team successful, develop a perspective on the talent market, and help our leaders make thoughtful hiring decisions. You’ll also have room to experiment, build with AI, and improve how we recruit. We’re looking for someone who’s excited by that mix of ownership, learning, and building.

Responsibilities:

Own Your Searches

 - Lead full-cycle recruiting from intake through offer and close, keeping searches organized and moving.

 - Partner with hiring managers to define what great looks like, calibrate early, and set realistic expectations around timing, compensation, and the market.

 - Run thoughtful screens that assess experience, skills, and motivation, and give hiring teams clear, specific recommendations.

 - Manage interview loops, keep feedback timely, and give candidates an honest understanding of the role and where they stand.

 - Understand what matters to each candidate and guide offer and closing conversations.

Find Great People

 - Build targeted outbound pipelines using LinkedIn Recruiter, Juicebox, research, and your own growing network.

 - Get creative about where you look and how you identify strong talent, especially when the obvious approach isn’t working.

 - Write personalized outreach that gives someone a real reason to respond.

 - Stay connected with strong candidates beyond a single opening and build relationships we can return to as Savvy grows.

Bring a Point of View

 - Learn how our teams operate, what they’re trying to accomplish, and how each hire contributes.

 - Turn market research and candidate conversations into useful advice for hiring managers.

 - Speak up when scope, level, compensation, or the interview process is getting in the way of a successful search, and recommend a path forward.

Make Us Better

 - Use Claude and other AI tools in your daily work to research, source, and improve recruiting workflows. Share what works with the team.

 - Use pipeline data to understand what’s working, spot bottlenecks, and adjust your approach.

 - Keep Ashby accurate and up to date so the team can trust the pipeline and reporting.

 - Contribute to projects across referrals, employer branding, tooling, structured interviewing, and candidate experience.

Must Have:

 - Recruiting experience whether at an agency, a VC firm’s talent team, or in-house. We’re open to different paths and would love to meet someone making their first move into an internal recruiting role.

 - Experience owning searches or significant parts of the recruiting process, with an eagerness to take on full-cycle responsibility.

 - A strong sourcing foundation. You know how to research a market, find great people, and build relationships through thoughtful outreach.

 - The curiosity to learn unfamiliar roles and understand what makes someone successful in them. You don’t need to have recruited for every function we support.

 - The ability to understand candidates’ motivations, build trust, and help them navigate career decisions.

 - Clear, thoughtful communication with candidates, hiring partners, and teammates.

 - Strong follow-through and organization. You keep people informed, details accurate, and searches moving.

 - Good judgment about when to take initiative, ask for help, or flag a problem.

 - Resourcefulness and excitement about using AI to improve how you work, wherever you are in learning to use it.

 - We offer a generous relocation package to help top talent make the move to our NYC office

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

jobs.title: Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

LEGAL COUNSEL

Based on site at Rocket Lab's Headquarters in Long Beach, CA, this Legal Counsel will play a key role in supporting the Legal Department and functional and program management teams across the organization. This role is ideal for an early to mid-level attorney with experience in contract drafting and negotiations, dispute resolution, and regulatory compliance. The successful candidate will provide strategic legal advice for a publicly traded company performing U.S. Government contracts, to ensure compliance and support the company’s growth and innovation.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

Managing contractual and operational legal matters for the company, as well as providing legal support for litigation and other compliance matters. This includes:

Commercial and Government Contracts (Sales, Procurement, Operations):

• Draft, review, and negotiate a broad range of agreements, including prime contracts with the US Government and subcontracts for work under US government prime contracts, Master Service Agreements, IP licensing, non-disclosure agreements, real property leases and strategic partnership agreements.

• Create and implement contract playbooks, fallback positions, templates, and clause libraries to streamline cycles.

• Collaborate with business teams to balance risk with speed-to-value; maintain visibility into obligations and renewals.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Enablement:

• Partner with Finance (pricing, revenue recognition, indemnities/limitations), IT/Security (data protection and controls), HR (employment matters), and Operations (Supply Chain, quality and logistics).

• Design and execute legal due diligence plans covering contracts, operations, IP, privacy/security, labor & employment, environmental, anti-bribery/anti-corruption, sanctions/export controls, material contracts, and litigation.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school.

• Active membership in the California State Bar or Registered In-House Counsel (RIHC).

• Minimum of 5 years of legal experience.

• Proven experience as in-house counsel or at a top-tier law firm.

• Experience in negotiating contracts, non-disclosure agreements and IP licenses.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to articulate and effectively communicate information to various levels of management and program teams.

• Ability to obtain a DoD Top Secret security clearance.

• Domestic and International travel as necessary to support business needs.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• 7+ years of experience strongly preferred.

• Extensive knowledge of Government contracts and contract types, the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation (DFAR).

• Experience supporting DoD and NASA prime contracts and/or subcontracts supporting DoD and NASA programs.

• Familiarity with the compliance requirements of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and the Export Administration Regulations.

• Demonstrate initiative and the ability to take on greater responsibilities with potential for leadership opportunities over time.

• Capable of adapting to fast-paced changes, shifting priorities, evolving directions, and addressing unique legal challenges.

• Experience managing external counsel relationships and budgets, focusing on reviewing legal bills and keeping costs under control.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$162,800—$217,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   


THE ROLE

Savvy is hiring our first dedicated developer experience engineer. Coding agents are already part of how our engineers work, but adoption has moved faster than our ability to make their output consistently good. Wrong code and weak architectural decisions still create review burden. We are hiring someone to treat that as an engineering problem, not solve it with a longer prompt.

You will own how developers across EPD interact with coding agents and with the systems around them. That includes the codebase itself, our internal skills and instructions, cloud coding workflows, agentic code review, CI, local development, testing, debugging, and delivery. You will have substantial autonomy to make cross-cutting decisions, change defaults, and set standards across the organization.

 

This is a hands-on platform engineering role. Most of your time will be spent building software and improving the environment in which developers and agents work. You will also talk directly with engineers, study where time and quality are being lost, test your ideas against real work, and help teams adopt better ways of operating. You will join our infrastructure and harness team and partner closely with infrastructure, security, data, and product engineers.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own developer and agent experience: Set the roadmap for how our engineers and coding agents navigate the codebase, use internal tools, run tests, review changes, and ship software.

 - Build the cloud coding experience: Build the developer-facing layer around our existing compute foundations, including task intake, environment setup, context, tools, permissions, observability, review, and delivery.

 - Improve agent output at the source: Change repository structure, interfaces, documentation, instructions, and feedback loops so agents produce correct code and sound architecture more consistently.

 - Engineer context deliberately: Design what agents receive up front, discover progressively, persist, compact, hand off, or discard. Choose models and reasoning effort based on evidence from the job, not habit.

 - Own our internal skills system: Raise the quality of our shared skills and instructions through clear contribution standards, evaluation, discoverability, progressive disclosure, maintenance, and pruning.

 - Fix everyday developer friction: Improve CI speed and reliability, local setup, testing, debugging, deploy workflows, and the other bottlenecks that cost engineers time.

 - Measure what works: Combine developer research and satisfaction data with DORA or SPACE measures and task-level agent evaluations. Inspect traces, establish baselines, and test whether changes improve correctness, reviewability, cost, latency, and human intervention.

 - Drive adoption: Work directly with engineers, teach effective practices, and turn successful experiments into defaults. When the root problem is the codebase or engineering process, make that case and help fix it.

 - Partner on safe autonomy: Work with our infrastructure and security engineers on sandboxing, credentials, approvals, auditability, and the controls needed to give cloud agents useful access without giving them unlimited access.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Exceptional with coding agents: You use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar tools for substantial work and can show how you decompose tasks, manage context, choose models, inspect failures, and consistently produce maintainable software. Faster output alone is not the bar.

 - Internal tools with real users: You have built developer tooling or a platform that engineers beyond your immediate team relied on. You learned from their behavior and support burden, not only from what they said they wanted.

 - CI or large-codebase experience: You have made a meaningful improvement to CI, testing, repository workflows, or developer productivity in a substantial, long-lived codebase.

 - Product judgment for internal systems: You can interview developers, separate symptoms from root causes, turn evidence into a roadmap, and say no to attractive work that will not improve the system.

 - Strong software engineering: You have built and operated substantial production software. We are open on language and framework, but you must be able to move from diagnosis to a durable implementation yourself.

 - Evaluation over intuition: You know that agent behavior is nondeterministic and changing quickly. You compare prompts, context, tools, models, and workflows against representative tasks rather than declaring success from a demo.

 - Cross-team influence: You can set standards and change defaults across teams without becoming a gatekeeper. You explain the evidence, earn trust, and remain accountable for the experience you create.

 - Pragmatic range: You are comfortable moving between platform code, repository conventions, evaluation data, developer interviews, documentation, and hands-on enablement. This is not a prompt-writing, DevRel, or framework-only role.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building cloud or remote development environments, coding-agent control planes, or secure execution sandboxes.

 - Experience building or operating an agentic code review system.

 - Experience designing agent tools, skills, context systems, memory, orchestration, or model-routing infrastructure.

 - Experience using DORA, SPACE, or similar frameworks without reducing developer productivity to a single metric.

 - Experience in financial services or another security- and compliance-sensitive environment.

jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER I – PCBA

Based onsite at Pasadena, the Senior Global Supply Manager will play a pivotal role in the development and manufacture of advanced spaceflight hardware for Rocket Lab Robotics. Rocket Lab Robotics designs and manufactures robotic systems, precision electromechanical mechanisms, motion control electronics, optomechanical assemblies, and other high-reliability spacecraft components. You'll lead sourcing strategies, manage critical supplier relationships, and drive supply chain resilience across your assigned commodities and supplier portfolios. From early development to recurring flight production, you'll collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams to deliver world-class results in a high-mix, low-volume aerospace environment. This is a senior individual contributor position with significant supplier and commodity management responsibility but no direct personnel management responsibilities.

Rocket Lab's Supply Chain team is the backbone of our operations, ensuring the seamless flow of materials, components, and products that power our missions. From managing procurement to ensuring compliance and quality, this team is critical to the success of our Electron & Neutron rockets and Space Systems programs.

WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

• Develop and execute sourcing strategies for assigned commodities, components, assemblies, and manufacturing services (including precision machining, PCBAs, electronics, and electromechanical hardware) that balance cost, quality, capacity, delivery, and supply continuity.

• Identify, evaluate, qualify, and develop suppliers capable of meeting complex technical requirements, supporting everything from engineering prototypes and qualification hardware to recurring production.

• Serve as the primary commercial and strategic interface with critical domestic and international suppliers, building strong long-term relationships.

• Lead supplier negotiations on pricing, lead times, delivery commitments, and commercial terms, and support the development of supplier agreements within delegated authority.

• Analyze supplier quotations, cost structures, and manufacturing processes to identify cost savings and avoidance opportunities, and track sourcing performance and pricing trends.

• Drive continuous improvement in supplier performance through metrics, performance reviews, and supplier recovery plans.

• Review drawings, specifications, and BOMs, and work with Engineering and Manufacturing on manufacturability, alternate materials and processes, make-versus-buy decisions, and the transition of prototype designs into repeatable production sourcing.

• Identify and mitigate supply chain risks, especially for long-lead, critical, and single-source components, and develop contingency plans for shortages, supplier performance issues, and demand changes.

• Partner with Quality Assurance and Supplier Quality Engineering on supplier qualification, audits, corrective actions, and compliance with AS9100, export control, traceability, and counterfeit-part prevention requirements.

• Coordinate with Sourcing Specialists, Production Control, Program Management, and Finance to turn sourcing strategies into purchase orders, secure delivery commitments, and resolve critical supplier issues.

• Support business development and proposal activities with supplier quotations, cost estimates, and lead-time assessments.

• Mentor Sourcing Specialists and less-experienced team members, share commodity knowledge and best practices, and act as the go-to procurement expert in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

• 5+ years of experience in procurement, sourcing or supplier management.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of work experience (9+ years of total work experience).

• Demonstrated experience independently managing complex supplier relationships and sourcing technically complex components, assemblies, or manufacturing services.

• Proven experience negotiating pricing, lead times, and commercial agreements, and analyzing supplier quotations and manufacturing costs.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production requirements, and material supply constraints, and experience working with Engineering and Manufacturing to resolve technical sourcing challenges.

• Experience identifying and mitigating supplier risks related to cost, delivery, capacity, or quality.

• Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and procurement processes.

• Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple critical suppliers across concurrent programs.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE

• Experience sourcing for spacecraft, robotics, precision mechanisms, or electromechanical systems.

• Experience managing suppliers of precision machined components, PCBAs, electronic components, or specialized aerospace hardware.

• Experience in high-mix, low-volume aerospace manufacturing and recurring flight hardware production, or in a rapid-growth environment with constantly shifting priorities.

• Strong ability to read and interpret drawings, with technical familiarity with CNC machining, electronics manufacturing, precision assembly, and design for manufacturing.

• Experience developing and negotiating long-term supplier agreements and strategic sourcing arrangements.

• Experience managing long-lead materials, single-source suppliers, and complex supply chain risks.

• Experience supporting engineering prototype development, qualification hardware, and new product introduction.

• Experience with AS9100, export controls, FAR/DFARS requirements, material traceability, and counterfeit electronic component prevention.

• Professional certification such as CPSM, APICS CSCP, or equivalent.

• Exceptional organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize and multi-task across multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across all functions and levels of the organization.

• Highly self-motivated, able to learn quickly and maintain the highest levels of quality and integrity.

• Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 10% of the time.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$94,400—$118,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. jobs.title: Senior Client Associate (West Coast)
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   

The Role:
The Savvy team is looking for an experienced Senior Client Associate who is ready to apply  their exceptional client service skills to drive impact in a fast-paced and growing environment. In this role, you’ll serve as a dedicated operational partner to multiple advisors, ensuring their clients receive exceptional day-to-day support. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, an  excellent problem-solver, and a strong communicator who can help foster long-term client  relationships. 



This role will be critical in shaping our standard operating procedures and  ensuring we set the highest standard for client and advisor support. As an early member of the  Savvy team, you will help build out the client servicing function. You will also work closely with  the Product and Operations teams to shape the future roadmap of Savvy's product and advisory services.



Responsibilities: 

 - Responsible for day-to-day operations and administrative support of Savvy wealth  managers, providing exceptional client service and fostering long-term client relationships.

 - Own best-in-class execution of all client tasks, requests and inquiries in a timely manner.

 - Proactively seek out opportunities to improve Savvy's internal procedures in pursuit of the best advisor and client experience.

 - Streamline new client prospecting, closing, and onboarding processes including meeting preparation, obtaining account and investment strategy documentation, and driving account creation and transfers.

 - Assist advisors by executing investment transactions and fulfilling account billing & performance reporting tasks.

 - Work closely with other professional advisors such as CPAs, estate planning attorneys, business managers, insurance agents, and more.

 - Create and maintain client data in Salesforce and other systems.

 - Ensure Savvy is adhering to all required compliance policies and procedures.

 - Protect clients by maintaining confidentiality of all personal and financial information.
   
   

Must Have:

 - 2+ years of experience in a similar role with a registered investment advisory firm and/or broker-dealer including experience interacting directly with clients AND advisors.

 - A high-energy, collaborative, and self-starter attitude; willing to roll up your sleeves and have an incredible ownership mentality.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

 - Strong technical skills in Google Suite applications--Word, Excel, and Powerpoint-- and familiarity with the MS Office equivalents.

 - Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to prioritize and juggle multiple tasks at once.

 - Adept at quickly learning and adopting new technologies.



Nice to have:

 - Series 7 and 66 or Series 65 licenses.

 - BA/BS degree in finance, economics, or related field.

 - Advanced degrees or designations such as CFP, CPA, CFA

 - Prior experience using Salesforce

 - Prior experience working with custodians such as Fidelity, Charles Schwab, or Pershing Advisor Services



Additional Information:

Savvy Wealth is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that values diversity and individual contributions.


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - We offer a generous relocation package to help top talent make the move to our NYC office

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

 - Company 401(k) (including Mega backdoor Roth options), Commuter, and HSA/FSA plans 

 - NYC office in Union Square

 - Lunch and snacks provided in the office, & dinner if you stay late

 - Access to virtual mental health care (Spring Health) and health concierge (Rightway) to help you find the right care

 - Access to counseling for stress management, dependent care, nutrition, fitness, legal, and financial issues (Guardian WorkLifeMatters EAP)

 - Benefits are available to full-time employees

jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   


THE ROLE

Savvy is hiring our first dedicated agentic harness engineer. Coding agents are already part of how our engineers work, but adoption has moved faster than our ability to make their output consistently good. Wrong code and weak architectural decisions still create review burden. We are hiring someone to treat that as an engineering problem, not solve it with a longer prompt.

You will own how developers across EPD interact with coding agents and with the systems around them. That includes the codebase itself, our internal skills and instructions, cloud coding workflows, agentic code review, CI, local development, testing, debugging, and delivery. You will have substantial autonomy to make cross-cutting decisions, change defaults, and set standards across the organization.

 

This is a hands-on platform engineering role. Most of your time will be spent building software and improving the environment in which developers and agents work. You will also talk directly with engineers, study where time and quality are being lost, test your ideas against real work, and help teams adopt better ways of operating. You will join our infrastructure and harness team and partner closely with infrastructure, security, data, and product engineers.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own developer and agent experience: Set the roadmap for how our engineers and coding agents navigate the codebase, use internal tools, run tests, review changes, and ship software.

 - Build the cloud coding experience: Build the developer-facing layer around our existing compute foundations, including task intake, environment setup, context, tools, permissions, observability, review, and delivery.

 - Improve agent output at the source: Change repository structure, interfaces, documentation, instructions, and feedback loops so agents produce correct code and sound architecture more consistently.

 - Engineer context deliberately: Design what agents receive up front, discover progressively, persist, compact, hand off, or discard. Choose models and reasoning effort based on evidence from the job, not habit.

 - Own our internal skills system: Raise the quality of our shared skills and instructions through clear contribution standards, evaluation, discoverability, progressive disclosure, maintenance, and pruning.

 - Fix everyday developer friction: Improve CI speed and reliability, local setup, testing, debugging, deploy workflows, and the other bottlenecks that cost engineers time.

 - Measure what works: Combine developer research and satisfaction data with DORA or SPACE measures and task-level agent evaluations. Inspect traces, establish baselines, and test whether changes improve correctness, reviewability, cost, latency, and human intervention.

 - Drive adoption: Work directly with engineers, teach effective practices, and turn successful experiments into defaults. When the root problem is the codebase or engineering process, make that case and help fix it.

 - Partner on safe autonomy: Work with our infrastructure and security engineers on sandboxing, credentials, approvals, auditability, and the controls needed to give cloud agents useful access without giving them unlimited access.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Exceptional with coding agents: You use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar tools for substantial work and can show how you decompose tasks, manage context, choose models, inspect failures, and consistently produce maintainable software. Faster output alone is not the bar.

 - Internal tools with real users: You have built developer tooling or a platform that engineers beyond your immediate team relied on. You learned from their behavior and support burden, not only from what they said they wanted.

 - CI or large-codebase experience: You have made a meaningful improvement to CI, testing, repository workflows, or developer productivity in a substantial, long-lived codebase.

 - Product judgment for internal systems: You can interview developers, separate symptoms from root causes, turn evidence into a roadmap, and say no to attractive work that will not improve the system.

 - Strong software engineering: You have built and operated substantial production software. We are open on language and framework, but you must be able to move from diagnosis to a durable implementation yourself.

 - Evaluation over intuition: You know that agent behavior is nondeterministic and changing quickly. You compare prompts, context, tools, models, and workflows against representative tasks rather than declaring success from a demo.

 - Cross-team influence: You can set standards and change defaults across teams without becoming a gatekeeper. You explain the evidence, earn trust, and remain accountable for the experience you create.

 - Pragmatic range: You are comfortable moving between platform code, repository conventions, evaluation data, developer interviews, documentation, and hands-on enablement. This is not a prompt-writing, DevRel, or framework-only role.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building cloud or remote development environments, coding-agent control planes, or secure execution sandboxes.

 - Experience building or operating an agentic code review system.

 - Experience designing agent tools, skills, context systems, memory, orchestration, or model-routing infrastructure.

 - Experience using DORA, SPACE, or similar frameworks without reducing developer productivity to a single metric.

 - Experience in financial services or another security- and compliance-sensitive environment.


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - We offer a generous relocation package to help top talent make the move to our NYC office

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

 - Company 401(k) (including Mega backdoor Roth options), Commuter, and HSA/FSA plans 

 - NYC office in Union Square

 - Lunch and snacks provided in the office, & dinner if you stay late

 - Access to virtual mental health care (Spring Health) and health concierge (Rightway) to help you find the right care

 - Benefits are available to full-time employees

jobs.title: Global Program Operations Head (GPOH)
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Tango Therapeutics is a biotechnology company dedicated to discovering novel drug targets and delivering the next generation of precision medicine for the treatment of cancer.

Using an approach that starts and ends with patients, Tango leverages the genetic principle of synthetic lethality to discover and develop therapies that take aim at critical targets in cancer.

This includes expanding the universe of precision oncology targets into novel areas such as tumor suppressor gene loss and their contribution to the ability of cancer cells to evade immune cell killing.

The Tango labs and offices are located at 201 Brookline Avenue, in the Fenway area of Boston, Massachusetts.

Summary

We are seeking a Global Program Operations Head (GPOH), reporting into the Vice President, Clinical Operations, to lead the strategic and operational execution of a portfolio of clinical trials within a designated disease area. This role partners cross-functionally with Clinical, Medical, Regulatory, and Operational Excellence to ensure programs are aligned with corporate goals, regulatory requirements, and operational feasibility.

You will drive program-level strategy, oversee trial execution, and manage Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and external vendors, ensuring delivery against timelines, budgets, and quality expectations. Additionally, you will lead and develop a high-performing clinical operations team while supporting governance, risk management, and inspection readiness in a fast-paced biotech environment.

Your Role

• Oversee the strategic and operational execution of a portfolio of clinical trials within a designated disease area

• Ensure alignment with corporate goals and regulatory standards

• Represent Global Clinical Operations in Global Program Teams (GPTs) and sub-teams, contributing to program-level strategy and operational planning

• Collaborate with Medical and Regulatory Directors to ensure clinical strategies are scientifically sound, meet regulatory requirements, and are operationally feasible

• Partner with Operational Excellence & Clinical Compliance to align on risk assessment, trial- and site management metrics, KPIs, and KRIs

• Define and implement outsourcing strategies in partnership with the VP of Global Clinical Operations and Head of Clinical Sourcing & Contracting

• Lead the selection, negotiation, contracting, and performance oversight of CROs and external vendors

• Monitor trial progress and key deliverables, guiding Clinical Trial Teams (CTTs) in execution planning, issue resolution, and risk mitigation

• Manage program and trial budgets, ensuring accurate forecasting, cost control, and financial accountability

• Track CRO/ vendor performance using metrics, KPIs, KRIs and participate in governance meetings to address escalated issues and drive continuous improvement

• Provide regular updates on trial progress to internal governance bodies, including GPT and Executive Leadership Team

• Support inspection readiness activities and represent the organization during Health Authority inspections

• Provide leadership, coaching, and performance management to Clinical Trial Leaders (CTLs), Clinical Contract Managers (CTMs), Clinical Trial Specialists (CTSs), and Site Management Leader (SMLs)

• Set clear objectives, deliver ongoing feedback, and develop tailored development plans to support team growth and capability building

• Oversee hiring, onboarding, and training of new team members, fostering a culture of operational excellence and continuous learning

What You Bring

• 12+ years of trial management experience with 7+ years in leadership position

• Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy or related field (required). Advanced degree, e.g., MS, PharmD, PhD, MBA (preferred).

• Significant experience working in global clinical development organization

• Experience in Oncology development (preferred)

• Direct experience with health authority inspections (FDA, EMA, MHRA, etc.) incl. sponsor GCP inspections

• Significant experience in outsourcing and oversight

• Expert knowledge in ICH-GCP, FDA guidelines, EU CTR and other relevant guidelines

• Expert knowledge in financial planning, tracking, and reporting

• Expert knowledge in risk assessment and management on program and trial-level

• Executive presence and strategic thinking on corporate-, program-, and trial-level

• Strong decision‑making and sound judgment

• Strong leadership and interpersonal skills

• High credibility with senior leadership

• Familiarity with clinical trial systems (e.g., CTMS, eTMF, EDC, IRT, eCOA) and operational metrics, KPIs, and KRIs

• Willingness to travel, as required (typically 10–20%)

Because we’re a technology company at heart, you’ll do it with AI and automation at the center, building the workflows that let one strategist deliver coverage that takes a whole team at a legacy firm. If you’ve been an investment strategist or portfolio manager at an RIA, a portfolio consultant at a wirehouse, or a client portfolio manager at an asset manager and want to build something with a direct line to growth, this is the seat.

 - Use AI and internal tools to identify opportunities, scale portfolio reviews, and speed up proposal generation

 - Partner with Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD), Marketing, and Advisor Success to improve advisor support, tooling, and execution

 - Bring advisor feedback back to SWIM leadership to refine offerings, messaging, and growth strategy




MUST HAVE:

jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is seeking an experienced Senior Estimator / Cost Manager to serve as the primary day-to-day client interface on large, mission-critical construction programs within the US Electric Vehicle (EV) and transportation infrastructure sector. You will provide commercial leadership during design and construction, supporting the delivery of complex EV facilities and depots featuring infrastructure-heavy works, MEP-intensive buildings, and fleet-charging systems.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, confident in client-facing environments, and able to work independently within integrated project teams while upholding Turner & Townsend’s standards for commercial governance.

This role offers US remote flexibility, though proximity to the SF Bay Area for local stakeholder engagement is a strong advantage.

Responsibilities:

• Establish and maintain robust cost control, change management, and commercial governance processes.
• Estimate, review, negotiate, and manage change orders throughout the construction lifecycle.
• Review contractor and subcontractor pricing for accuracy, entitlement, and value for money, leading negotiations on behalf of the client where required.
• Manage contingency, commitment tracking, cost-to-complete forecasting, and cost variance analysis.
• Perform post-contract quantity surveying, cost control, valuations, and payment certification.

• Ensure final accounts are negotiated, agreed, and closed out in a timely and defensible manner.

• Collaborate with owners, project managers, design teams, and contractors to support cost development and design progression.
• Inform and influence engineering and design priorities by assessing and communicating cost, risk, and schedule impacts.
• Coordinate all sources of cost data, including GC submissions, subcontractor pricing, supplier inputs, direct procurement, and quantities from A/Es.
• Participate in value engineering and design optioneering exercises, supporting cost optimization without compromising performance or schedule.
• Prepare funding data, executive cost presentations, and reporting materials for stakeholder review.
• Support commercial management of infrastructure-intensive and operationally critical systems, including:Electrical distribution and utility upgradesMEP-heavy building systemsSite works, civil packages, and phased constructionEV charging and fleet-support infrastructure integrated into facility environments
• Manage cost and change implications associated with phased delivery, fast-track construction, and evolving operational requirements.
• Produce accurate monthly cost reports, forecasts, and commercial dashboards for client presentation.
• Utilize internal systems to manage commission financial performance, margins, and resource forecasting.
• Implement and maintain Turner & Townsend Business Management Systems and delivery methodologies.

• Proven experience delivering cost management services on medium to large, complex construction projects within transportation, industrial, infrastructure, or mission-critical environments.
• Background in construction consultancy or client-side cost management strongly preferred.
• Strong knowledge of US construction contracts, procurement routes, valuations, change control, and final account processes.
• Experience supporting MEP-intensive works, infrastructure packages, and utility-driven construction scope.
